bodyText: **Router never mounted — endpoint unreachable** The `webhooks` Router is exported but never imported or mounted in `server/api.ts` (the only file that creates the Express `app`). A `POST /api/webhooks/github` request will receive a 404 because the route is never registered with the application. `app.use(webhooks)` (or equivalent) needs to be added in `api.ts`.

**No HMAC signature verification** GitHub App webhooks attach an `X-Hub-Signature-256` header containing an HMAC-SHA256 digest of the raw request body, keyed with the webhook secret. This handler accepts any POST request without verifying that header, so any HTTP client can send a forged payload and have it treated as a legitimate GitHub event. The raw body must be read before JSON parsing and the `crypto.timingSafeEqual` comparison must pass before processing any action.

excerpt: **`void` expressions are no-ops — feature logic is unimplemented**
bodyText: **`void` expressions are no-ops — feature logic is unimplemented** `void oauthRedirectAllowlist` and `void ENABLED_ACTIONS` evaluate the expressions and discard the result; they are equivalent to a no-op and exist only to suppress unused-variable linting errors. Neither the redirect allowlist nor the per-action feature toggles are actually consulted anywhere in the handler, so the PR description's claims ("reads OAuth2 redirect allowlist", "per-action feature toggles") describe behaviour that isn't present in this diff. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

excerpt: **`req.body` is always `undefined` — every webhook silently returns 200 ignored**
bodyText: **`req.body` is always `undefined` — every webhook silently returns 200 ignored** `api.ts` creates the Express `app` without registering `express.json()` (or any body-parsing middleware). Without it, Express leaves `req.body` as `undefined`, so `(req.body as { action?: string })?.action` always evaluates to `undefined`, `action` is coerced to `""`, and `decideWebhookResponse("")` always returns `{ status: 200, body: { ignored: true } }`. Even after the router is mounted, every real `pull_request` event will be silently dropped instead of queued with a 202.
